objective: Test whether making the baseline/text blend weight adapt to market regime improves the V16 signal: higher cumulative excess, better IC, and no worse drawdown.
motivation: V16 uses a fixed 65/35 baseline/text blend regardless of market state. Event-driven text signals plausibly work better in up markets and worse in down markets, so a fixed weight may leave value on the table.

architecture_change.regime_definition: prior rebalance period benchmark return (no look-ahead)
architecture_change.note: Training is unchanged (reuses the frozen V16 models); only the score combination is restructured.

gates.v19_excess_beats_v16_ungated: excess above the frozen V16 ungated +5.92pp
gates.v19_beats_same_run_v16: excess above the same-run V16 control
gates.v19_drawdown_no_worse: max drawdown no worse than the same-run V16 control
gates.v19_ic5_positive: rank IC5 turns positive (the decisive gate)

decision_rule.all_gates_passed: the adaptive blend replaces the fixed blend as the preferred representation; still no execution and still requires shadow testing
decision_rule.any_gate_failed: decision stays keep_v6; result recorded as retrospective evidence

honest_reporting: the three regime weights are one preregistered configuration, not an optimized fit
2020-2025 is a retrospective window reused by V3-V18
historical evidence suggests the IC5-positive gate will fail
this restructures the score combination, not the underlying predictive signal
